questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Fo find a destination that had exciting oppotunities- culture, food, history. 
And to find a destination that was not too far away from Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Somewhat easy.

The OLA was a bit complicated.
But all mails we  recived with deadlines and so on was helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Not so much assistance.
No kind of official introduction because the trimester at the political science faculty - university of Milan -started much earlier than other faculties. So the introduction was too late for us who have been here for more than one month.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Massimo Costa, the erasmus coordinator at university of Milan was kind and answered quickly on emails.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found a room in a shared apartment through websites.
spotahome.com

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is more dificult to find something off campuss that can match the prices of on campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I live with 3 other international students that I didn't know before, and sometimes there was problems, but not anything huge.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to register for courses myself, and register for exams. We had a "guideline" how to do it, so it was easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: "how to" guides online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: just follow the guides, its easy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Some courses were easier than in Denmark, some was the same level i would say. 
Very different structure and system.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Not many exercises during class, as I am just to on economics in Denmark. 
Whe exams were also very loose, many students did not take it serious a cheated. 
No exam-guards, and nothing about to put bags and phones away as we are used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. trimester jan-mar
Data-driven economic analysis
Economics of Inequality

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
2. trimester apr-jun 
Governments and the global economy 
International monetary policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I find all my courses for relevant. 

Economics of inequality was easy if you are used to using STATA.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were several oppotunities to engage in activities on campus, BUT every email about such things was in Italian, so difficult to know which one is important.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the app Dice.  Here you can find a lot of different events in Milan.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
to on trips to other cities, eg. Verona, Bergamo, Como, 
Hiking tours near Lake Como 

I visited Rome for a weekend, went by train. Very easy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy,

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn's got many local friends. But just be open and ask to go to apperitivo or coffee together

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the late dining, and culture with apperetivo

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open in the beginning to find new friends. Even though it can be challanging, it is fun to hang out with others. 
The system is very loose, so if you are confused about anything, just ask, or send emails to the professors.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and hang out with. The many coffees before and after school where we were studying together.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
My living situation. 
We has problems in my apartment, and no one took responsibility for anything, and that caused some problems.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
